title: Asymmetrical Flow Field-Flow Fractionation for Sizing of Gold Nanoparticles in Suspension
protocol: Assemble the AF4 cartridge and connect all hardware components of the AF4 system and the UV-vis detector following the manufacturer’s manual.
Install all necessary software packages for control, data acquisition, processing, and evaluation as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Ensure that all signal connections between the AF4 system and the UV-vis detector are tight without leakages.
Flush the setup with ultrapure water (UPW) for 15 min at a tip flow rate of 1 mL∙min-1, focus flow rate of 1 mL∙min-1, and cross flow rate of 1.5 mL∙min-1.
Tighten the respective connectors if necessary and repeat the procedure until no leakages are observable.
Monitor the internal system pressure during all measurements to ensure it remains within 4 to 12 bar.
Adjust the backpressure tubing if the pressure is higher or lower than the specified range.
Ensure that the channel pressure trend is constant throughout the entire measurement time.
Set the temperature of a channel oven to 25 °C, if available, to maintain comparable conditions for all AF4 experiments.
Add 8 g of solid sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and 2 g of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) to 1 L of UPW.
Stir the solution until total dissolution.
Add 500 μL of filtered surfactant mixture to 2 L of filtered and degassed UPW.
Vortex an arbitrary AuNP size standard (50 mg/L) for 2 min.
Dilute it 1:4 with UPW to obtain a final mass concentration of 12.5 mg/L.
Vortex the suspension for additional 2 min after dilution to homogenize.
Use software settings described to flush system with cleaning solution for 30 min.
Change eluent bottle and flush system with UPW for 20 min.
Replace inline pump filters.
Open AF4 cartridge and replace AF4 membrane.
Reassemble AF4 cartridge and reconnect it with the AF4-UV-vis system.
Flush cleaned AF4-UV-vis system with eluent for at least 30 min to equilibrate membrane and stabilize system.
Check for potential leakages again.
Qualify AF4-UV-vis system by determining mass recovery and variation of retention time using AuNP size standard.
Perform direct injection run without application of separation force.
Create new measurement file by opening File | New | Run in the AF4 control software.
Define sample and measurement description as well as injection volume and sample name within the Run tab.
Set measurement parameters in FFF method according to Table 2.
Click on Run button to start measurement.
Perform fractionation run with application of a separation force (Cross flow).
Define the fractionation method using the conditions specified in Table 3.
Click on the Run button to start the measurement.
Perform the measurement in quadruplicate.
Vortex AuNP suspension (each 50 mg/L) for 2 minutes.
Dilute each AuNP suspension 1:4 with UPW to obtain a final mass concentration of 12.5 mg/L.
Vortex diluted suspensions again for 2 minutes to homogenize.
Prepare the unknown AuNP sample for analysis using the same procedure as for the calibration standards.
Enter the values from Table 2 into the manufacturer’s software to define the separation and sample parameters.
Press the Run button to start the direct injection measurement of all AuNP size standards using the AF4 method from Table 2.
Fractionate each AuNP size standard individually using the AF4 method displayed in Table 3.
Enter the values summarized in Table 3 into the manufacturer’s software at the appropriate positions.
Define the fractionation method by a focusing step, several elution steps, and a rinse step.
Press the Run button to start the experiment for fractionating each AuNP size standard.
Perform a direct injection measurement of the unknown AuNP sample using the AF4 method displayed in Table 2.
Conduct the fractionation of the unknown AuNP sample by performing the AF4 method listed in Table 3.
Store 50 mg∙L-1 AuNP stock suspensions at 4–8 °C before use.
Dilute AuNP suspensions ideally within 30 min prior to application.
Perform mass recovery calculation using data evaluation software provided by the AF4-UV-vis system manufacturer or spreadsheet analysis after exporting raw data from acquisition software.
Calculate AuNP mass recovery by comparing UV-vis peak areas of fractionation and direct injection measurements.
Use Beer-Lambert law to correlate peak area with AuNP mass in direct injection measurement.
Import dat. files obtained from both direct injection and fractionation runs.
Select the UV-vis detector trace in the Overview tab.
Define a Region of Interest (ROI) and baseline for all measurements.
Insert Direct Injection Calibration via Insert option.
Select all direct injection runs in the Direct Injection Calibration Settings view.
Enter a UV extinction coefficient for each selected run.
Establish the calibration line using the area under the UV-vis signal trace within the ROI and the injected amount calculated from the entered concentration and injection volume.
Assign the established calibration function to the respective fractionation measurements.
For each size standard and unknown AuNP sample, establish a separate calibration function due to size-dependent UV-vis absorbance.
Calculate quantitative results for analyses using data evaluation software or spreadsheet analysis after exporting raw data.
Calculate the variation of retention time using either data evaluation software or spreadsheet analysis.
Open the Overview window to display UV traces for all imported measurements.
Adjust peak detection parameters within the signal processing toolbox.
Extract peak maxima from measurement files.
Calculate relative standard deviation using a spreadsheet software.
Perform size determination using data evaluation software or spreadsheet analysis.
Export retention time at UV-vis peak maximum and void time from acquisition software.
Plot void time corrected retention times of AuNP size standards against their hydrodynamic sizes.
Select the UV-vis detector signal from the detectors list in the Overview tab.
Define a ROI and baseline for each measurement, which can be adjusted in the Signal and Baseline view.
Use the Signal processing toolbox on the right to smooth noisy signals.
Assign the calibration function to the measurements of the unknown AuNP sample by selecting respective fractionations within the Select Runs for Assignment list.
Display the results by opening a particle size distribution calculation within the insert tab.
Select the previously created particle size calibration for the unknown AuNP sample measurements.
Average all signals of one sample and list the result in the peak maximum label.
Plot the calibration line over the fractogram by selecting the Show calibration curve checkbox.
Generate a cumulative size distribution by selecting the Show cumulative distribution checkbox.
